name: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints
summary: Introduces grouped-query attention, sharing each key-value head across a group of query heads, and uptraining multi-head checkpoints into multi-query or grouped-query models.

name: Layer Normalization
summary: Proposes layer normalization, which normalizes summed inputs across the units of a layer for each training case, and applies it to recurrent networks.

name: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
summary: Introduces an encoder-decoder translation model with a learned soft alignment (additive attention) over source annotations instead of a single fixed-length vector.

name: Understanding Dropout
summary: Analyses dropout with a general formalism, deriving its averaging properties for linear and sigmoidal networks and its regularization behaviour.

name: Training with Noise is Equivalent to Tikhonov Regularization
summary: Shows that training with small input noise is, to first order, equivalent to adding a Tikhonov regularization term to the sum-of-squares error.

cited.version: author's re-typeset manuscript (Microsoft Research), not the version of record

name: Re-evaluating the Role of Bleu in Machine Translation Research
summary: Argues that improved Bleu scores are neither necessary nor sufficient for improved translation quality, with examples where Bleu disagrees with human judgments.

name: A Systematic Comparison of Smoothing Techniques for Sentence-Level BLEU
summary: Compares seven smoothing techniques for sentence-level BLEU and measures their correlation with human judgments.

name: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways
summary: Describes PaLM, a 540-billion-parameter dense decoder-only Transformer trained with the Pathways system, and reports its few-shot results.

name: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
summary: Presents an IO-aware exact attention algorithm that tiles computation to reduce reads and writes between GPU high-bandwidth memory and on-chip SRAM.

name: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
summary: Introduces BERT, a Transformer encoder pre-trained with masked language modelling and next-sentence prediction, then fine-tuned for downstream language understanding tasks.

name: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
summary: Introduces the Vision Transformer, which applies a standard Transformer encoder to sequences of image patches for image classification.

name: flax.nnx.Dropout (Flax NNX stochastic layers API reference)
summary: API reference for the Flax NNX Dropout module, documenting its rate, broadcast dimensions, deterministic flag and random-number stream arguments.

name: Results of WMT22 Metrics Shared Task: Stop Using BLEU – Neural Metrics Are Better and More Robust
summary: Reports the WMT22 metrics shared task, comparing automatic metrics against expert MQM judgments across language pairs and domains.

name: Dropout as a Bayesian Approximation: Representing Model Uncertainty in Deep Learning
summary: Casts dropout training in deep networks as approximate Bayesian inference in deep Gaussian processes and uses Monte Carlo dropout to estimate model uncertainty.

name: DropBlock: A regularization method for convolutional networks
summary: Proposes DropBlock, which drops contiguous regions of convolutional feature maps rather than independent units, with a schedule that increases the dropped fraction.

name: Deep Learning
summary: Textbook covering the mathematical background, modern practice and research topics of deep learning; Chapter 7 covers regularization, including dropout.

cited.version: online edition, Chapter 7 (Regularization for Deep Learning)

name: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
summary: Describes the Llama 3 models of 8B, 70B and 405B parameters: data, architecture, scaling, infrastructure, post-training, safety and evaluations, and experiments on image, video and speech.

name: Theoretical Limitations of Self-Attention in Neural Sequence Models
summary: Proves that self-attention models with hard or soft attention cannot model periodic finite-state languages or hierarchical structure unless layers or heads grow with input length.

name: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
summary: Introduces residual networks, in which stacked layers learn residual functions with identity shortcut connections, allowing much deeper networks to be trained.

name: Improving neural networks by preventing co-adaptation of feature detectors
summary: Introduces dropout, randomly omitting hidden units during training to prevent co-adaptation of feature detectors, and reports results on several benchmarks.

name: Deep Networks with Stochastic Depth
summary: Trains residual networks by randomly dropping entire residual blocks during training and using the full network at test time.

name: Attention is not Explanation
summary: Tests whether attention weights in recurrent NLP models provide faithful explanations, comparing them with gradient-based importance and adversarial attention distributions.

name: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
summary: Reports empirical power-law relations between language-model cross-entropy loss and model size, dataset size and training compute.

name: Dropout layer (Keras API reference)
summary: API reference for the Keras Dropout layer, documenting its rate, noise shape, seed and training arguments.

name: To Ship or Not to Ship: An Extensive Evaluation of Automatic Metrics for Machine Translation
summary: Evaluates how well automatic machine-translation metrics agree with human pairwise system rankings over a large collection of human judgments.

name: Statistical Significance Tests for Machine Translation Evaluation
summary: Describes bootstrap resampling methods for estimating confidence intervals and statistical significance of differences in BLEU scores.

name: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
summary: Describes a large deep convolutional network trained on ImageNet with ReLUs, GPU training, data augmentation and dropout in the fully connected layers.

name: Understanding the Disharmony between Dropout and Batch Normalization by Variance Shift
summary: Explains performance loss when dropout precedes batch normalization through a variance shift between training and inference, and proposes mitigations.

name: ORANGE: a Method for Evaluating Automatic Evaluation Metrics for Machine Translation
summary: Proposes ORANGE, which evaluates automatic MT metrics by how highly they rank reference translations among candidates, and introduces smoothed sentence-level BLEU.

name: Tangled up in BLEU: Reevaluating the Evaluation of Automatic Machine Translation Evaluation Metrics
summary: Shows that metric-human correlation in WMT evaluations is sensitive to outlier systems and examines how reliably metric score differences predict human judgments.

name: Introducing LLaMA: A foundational, 65-billion-parameter language model
summary: Meta AI's announcement of LLaMA on 24 February 2023: the model sizes, the release under a noncommercial licence for research use, and access by application.

name: Meta and Microsoft Introduce the Next Generation of Llama
summary: Meta's announcement of Llama 2 on 18 July 2023, free for research and commercial use, with Microsoft as a preferred partner.

name: Introducing Meta Llama 3: The most capable openly available LLM to date
summary: Meta's announcement of Llama 3 on 18 April 2024, with pretrained and instruction-tuned models of 8B and 70B parameters.

name: Introducing Llama 3.1: Our most capable models to date
summary: Meta's announcement of Llama 3.1 on 23 July 2024, with models of 8B, 70B and 405B parameters and a context length of 128K.

name: Llama 3.2: Revolutionizing edge AI and vision with open, customizable models
summary: Meta's announcement of Llama 3.2 on 25 September 2024: vision models of 11B and 90B parameters and lightweight text models of 1B and 3B.

name: The Llama 4 herd: The beginning of a new era of natively multimodal AI innovation
summary: Meta's announcement of Llama 4 Scout and Llama 4 Maverick on 5 April 2025, mixture-of-experts models with native multimodality, and a preview of Llama 4 Behemoth.

name: LLaMA Model Card
summary: The model card of LLaMA version 1 in Meta's llama repository: developer, dates, sizes, licence, intended use, training data and evaluations.

name: Llama 2 Community License Agreement
summary: The licence of Llama 2, version release date 18 July 2023, with its grant, its acceptable use policy and its clause on 700 million monthly active users.

name: Llama 3.1 Community License Agreement
summary: The licence of Llama 3.1, version release date 23 July 2024.

name: Llama 3.2 Community License Agreement
summary: The licence of Llama 3.2, version release date 25 September 2024.

name: Llama 3.3 Community License Agreement
summary: The licence of Llama 3.3, version release date 6 December 2024.

name: Llama 3.3 model card
summary: The model card of Llama 3.3 in Meta's llama-models repository: a 70B text model, its context length, training data, release date, licence and benchmarks.

name: Meta Llama 3 Community License Agreement
summary: The licence of Meta Llama 3, version release date 18 April 2024.

name: Llama 4 Community License Agreement
summary: The licence of Llama 4, version effective date 5 April 2025.

name: Llama 4 model card
summary: The model card of Llama 4 Scout and Llama 4 Maverick in Meta's llama-models repository: parameters, context length, training data, release date and licence.

name: Meta's LLaMa license is not Open Source
summary: The Open Source Initiative's statement of 20 July 2023 that the Llama 2 licence is not an Open Source licence under the Open Source Definition.

name: The Open Source AI Definition 1.0
summary: The Open Source Initiative's definition of an Open Source AI system: the freedoms to use, study, modify and share it, and the preferred form for making modifications.

name: Bleu: a Method for Automatic Evaluation of Machine Translation
summary: Proposes BLEU, an automatic machine-translation metric combining modified n-gram precisions against reference translations with a brevity penalty.

name: chrF: character n-gram F-score for automatic MT evaluation
summary: Proposes chrF, an automatic machine-translation metric based on character n-gram precision and recall combined in an F-score.

name: A Call for Clarity in Reporting BLEU Scores
summary: Shows that BLEU scores vary with unreported parameters such as tokenization and normalization, and introduces sacreBLEU for standardized reporting.

name: Using the Output Embedding to Improve Language Models
summary: Studies the output embedding of neural language models and proposes tying input and output embeddings, which reduces parameters and perplexity.

name: Train Short, Test Long: Attention with Linear Biases Enables Input Length Extrapolation
summary: Introduces ALiBi, which replaces position embeddings with distance-proportional linear biases on attention scores, allowing extrapolation to longer inputs than seen in training.

name: torch.nn.Dropout (PyTorch API reference)
summary: API reference for the PyTorch Dropout module, which zeroes input elements with probability p during training and scales outputs by 1/(1-p).

name: torch.nn.functional.dropout (PyTorch API reference)
summary: API reference for the PyTorch functional dropout operation, documenting its probability, training and in-place arguments.

name: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training
summary: Describes generative pre-training of a Transformer decoder language model on unlabeled text followed by discriminative fine-tuning on language understanding tasks.

name: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
summary: Describes GPT-2, Transformer language models trained on the WebText corpus, and evaluates their zero-shot performance on downstream tasks.

name: A Structured Review of the Validity of BLEU
summary: Structured review of published correlations between BLEU and human evaluations, assessing the evidence for using BLEU to evaluate MT and other NLP systems.

name: sacreBLEU
summary: Python reference implementation of BLEU, chrF and TER that computes scores on detokenized output and reports a version signature of its parameters.

name: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units
summary: Adapts byte-pair encoding to segment words into subword units so neural machine translation can handle rare and unseen words with a fixed vocabulary.

name: Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need
summary: Proposes multi-query attention, in which attention heads share a single set of keys and values, to reduce memory bandwidth in incremental decoding.

name: GLU Variants Improve Transformer
summary: Tests gated linear unit variants such as GEGLU and SwiGLU in Transformer feed-forward layers and compares their quality with ReLU and GELU.

name: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting
summary: Presents dropout, randomly dropping units and their connections during training and scaling weights at test time, with experiments across vision, speech, text and biology.

name: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding
summary: Introduces rotary position embedding, which encodes absolute position by rotating query and key vectors so attention scores depend on relative position.

name: Rethinking the Inception Architecture for Computer Vision
summary: Describes Inception-v3 design principles, including factorized convolutions, and introduces label smoothing as a regularizer for classifiers.

name: Efficient Object Localization Using Convolutional Networks
summary: Proposes a cascaded convolutional architecture for human pose estimation and spatial dropout, which drops entire feature maps instead of individual activations.

name: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
summary: Describes LLaMA, decoder-only language models of 7B to 65B parameters trained only on publicly available data, with their architecture, training data and benchmark results.

name: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
summary: Describes Llama 2, pretrained and chat models of 7B to 70B parameters, with their pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, RLHF, safety work and evaluations.

name: Attention Is All You Need
summary: Introduces the Transformer, an encoder-decoder architecture based solely on multi-head self-attention and feed-forward layers, evaluated on machine translation.

name: Dropout Training as Adaptive Regularization
summary: Shows that dropout in generalized linear models is approximately equivalent to an adaptive L2 regularizer scaled by the inverse diagonal Fisher information.

name: Regularization of Neural Networks using DropConnect
summary: Introduces DropConnect, which randomly sets a subset of network weights rather than activations to zero during training.

name: On Layer Normalization in the Transformer Architecture
summary: Analyses gradients at initialization for Post-LN and Pre-LN Transformers and shows that Pre-LN Transformers can be trained without learning-rate warm-up.

name: Recurrent Neural Network Regularization
summary: Shows how to apply dropout to LSTMs by dropping only non-recurrent connections, and reports results on language modelling, speech recognition and translation.

name: Root Mean Square Layer Normalization
summary: Proposes RMSNorm, which normalizes layer inputs by their root mean square without mean centring, reducing computation relative to layer normalization.

name: Open Source AI is the Path Forward
summary: Mark Zuckerberg's letter of 23 July 2024, published by Meta with Llama 3.1, arguing that open source AI is good for developers, for Meta and for the world.
